shared_elements: shallow low-relief carving on the broad front face
horizontal band or register dividing the composition
row of repeated rounded elements near the top
curved arm-like or limb-like relief lines
justification: Both are tall freestanding stone monoliths whose flat front face carries shallow relief organised into an upper zone of repeated rounded elements above a horizontal band, with larger motifs (a disc/ring and curving limb-like lines) below, which is a genuinely comparable compositional scheme. The manner of execution differs sharply, however: A is dark, heavily weathered and reduced to a few broad, blunt, almost abstract volumes, while B is pale, crisply cut and densely populated with legible profile animals and birds, so any resemblance stays at the level of overall format rather than hand or iconographic detail.
